review_findings: Slide 9 now isolates prefix normalization and permits changes to future-relative targets/evaluation support.
Slides 15 and 16 now mark only eight distal joints at eight future times as queries, with a neutral non-query state and assertions.
Slide 25 now constructs exact empirical intervals from sorted references and interval midpoints, marks midrank values, and identifies its narrow zero-tail interval.
Slide 26 now awards half credit for tied AUROC scores.

slide.title: Missing observations, training masks, and queries differ.
slide.subtitle: A confidence gate describes what was observed; a training mask deliberately removes an observed input.

rows: The pose estimate lacks sufficient support.
The prefix keeps validity indicators; missing targets are not scored.
A policy hides an otherwise observed xy token.
Coordinates are erased before causal filling and feature calculation.
The predictor is asked for a fixed future joint and time.
Queries do not depend on future confidence or target values.
Change every future coordinate and validity bit.
Predictions, masks, anchors, and normalization must stay unchanged.

slide.caption: Confidence ≥ 0.5 and separate 70% prefix/future support gates are study settings. Imputed values are never measured outcomes.
slide.notes: Offline future support defines which predictions can be evaluated. Prefix quality, alone, must determine any deployment-time abstention. Future-relative target centering and scoring support may change when the future is altered; predictor inputs and outputs must not.

slide.title: Real observation support determines each realized mask.
slide.subtitle: These examples use the first window in lexical source, sequence, and window order.

example.selection: First source, sequence, and window in lexical identity order; no performance criterion.

slide.caption: Green is visible; blue-green is protected; peach is artificially hidden; gray is naturally missing; navy is a future query.
slide.notes: Example identity: 0b5f99df08a8027895d0853be6bfdbb474cf5612e8cd83a3de9f26b421cd0423. All masks use seed 27. Row labels are BlazePose IDs. The full 16-joint support and identical eight-step suffix are shown, including natural missingness.

slide.title: Mask matching concerns both budget and geometry.
slide.subtitle: The anatomical and random-group policies share group sizes 4, 4, 2, 2 and four-sample time blocks.

example.selection: First source, sequence, and window in lexical identity order; no performance criterion.

slide.caption: The example hides 70 of 174 eligible tokens (40.2%). Reference joints and latest anchors remain visible.
slide.notes: The final structured block can be truncated to achieve the exact budget. These are budget-matched priorities, not guaranteed intact tubes. Motion policies reserve at least 20% of hidden tokens for uniform draws. The separate pattern-only diagnostic tests information carried by the mask itself.

slide.title: A two-sided tail asks what is unusual relative to normal.
slide.subtitle: The curve uses the first frozen calibration component, selected by its saved order.
slide.caption: The residual is log forecast MSE minus its normal prediction from prefix motion and missingness. Orange ticks mark 8 separate normal references.
slide.notes: The empirical mid-CDF is F=(0.5+number below+0.5×number tied)/(nC+1). The anomaly score is |2F−1|. A high score means unusual ease or difficulty after the declared nuisance reference, not a specific disease. The exact same schedule is fit for current posture.

slide.title: The main ranking endpoint compares paired within-fold scores.
slide.subtitle: AUROC is the probability that a randomly chosen abnormal source receives a higher score than a normal source.
payload: The locked two-sided posture-plus-velocity score is compared with negative persistence error, the low-motion baseline.
Only abnormal-normal pairs inside the same outer fold contribute. Folds are weighted by their available number of pairs.
The bootstrap resamples source components within fold and label, using the same draws for both methods.
slide.caption: An AUROC of 0.5 is chance ranking. AUROC does not define a diagnostic threshold or clinical operating point.
slide.notes: The 5,000 paired bootstrap draws condition on saved overlapping fits and unknown participant relationships. Pooled rankings, average precision with prevalence, and equal-fold results are secondary summaries. Average precision summarizes precision as the threshold changes and depends on abnormal-source prevalence.
